tex_content.html:
Proposition
[Fundamental group of finite-dimensional K(G,1) is torsionfree] ↗ def:k-g-1-space ↗ ex:lens-spaces 1. ch2:2.45\group Cellular Homology

If a finite-dimensional CW complex $X$ is a $K(G,1)$, then $G=\pi _1(X)$ is torsionfree.
Proof

\sketch A finite cyclic subgroup would give a finite-dimensional covering $K(\mathbb {Z}_m,1)$, but $H_{2r+1}(\mathbb {Z}_m)\cong \mathbb {Z}_m$ for all $r\geq 0$, contradicting finite dimensionality.

□
